newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME zinc rally seen continuing, stocks seen down.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc rally seen continuing, stocks seen down.

text.p: Zinc prices are likely to steam higher later on Tuesday after hitting a 4-1/2 year peak on the London Metal Exchange (LME), base metal traders said.
They also predicted that most LME metal stocks would post modest falls, when the stocks report is released at 0900 GMT.
"Everybody is hot about zinc. The Chinese are very keen about these numbers," a dealer for a European metal trading company said.
"Zinc will probably go up this afternoon," a senior dealer for another metal trading company said. "It's pretty strong."

Three-month LME zinc ploughed to a 4-1/2 year high on Monday of US$1,307 a tonne before settling $6.0 up on the day at $1,296. It was being quoted by regional dealers at 0200 GMT just a shade under $1,300 at $1,294/99 a tonne.
A zinc dealer for a Japanese trading house said the strong prices in London had lured out Chinese sellers.
"I think a few thousand tonnes of zinc from China will arrive soon in Singapore," the dealer said, adding the metal is being sold to take advantage of current high prices.
Base metal traders in Singapore said zinc has enough strength to barge past $1,300 again and pegged near-term resistance at around $1,315-$1,325 a tonne.

The dealers said they were closely monitoring zinc stocks in the LME's Singapore warehouse. The total volume of zinc in the city-state reached 5,600 tonnes last Friday, down 425 tonnes from the previous Tuesday's stocks report.
The traders were divided about the possible movement in zinc inventories later on Tuesday, but a Japanese trader said he saw the number dropping by about 1,000 tonnes.
LME copper stocks are seen dipping by between 1,000-3,000 tonnes while aluminium inventories are likely to drop by 2,000-3,000 tonnes, the dealers said.
"My feeling is that copper and aluminium should be slightly down," one trader said.
Traders said copper is unlikely to duplicate the 4,275-tonne fall seen in the LME report last Friday.
There were no reports of fresh shipments of copper arriving in Singapore warehouses, dealers said.
The volume of copper in the LME Singapore warehouse reached 55,000 tonnes last Friday, up 200 tonnes from the previous Tuesday's report.
LME copper and aluminium prices were little changed in Asian trade on Tuesday.
Three-month copper was quoted by regional dealers at 0200 GMT at $2,336/41 a tonne against the late quote in London on Monday of $2,336/40 a tonne.
Three-month aluminium was seen by the same dealers at 0200 GMT at $1,660/65 a tonne compared with the late quote on the LME yesterday of $1,661/64 a tonne.
